source.display_title: 06/01/2026 - James Hiza x Andrew Musial  — Closed

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter named. The lead came through a written application which the rep had read — 'because in the application form, I saw that ... you're acquiring oil and gas mineral rights' — and the prospect confirmed, 'I know I put some of the notes.'

prospect.name: James Hiza
prospect.occupation: Business owner — acquires oil and gas mineral rights. 'I'm the boss. I have my own company.' Travels to Texas frequently, usually driving, roughly eight hours a day for two days. States he could technically retire now.
prospect.family_status: Engaged to Casey, 39, eighteen years younger; her daughters are 6 and 12. His own children are grown, one son lives in Singapore; his ex-wife is from Helsinki and the children are dual citizens.
prospect.training_background: Division 1 soccer player on a top-five national programme, played semi-pro, coached for twenty years and played three days a week into his forties. Always hated conventional gym work — 'I absolutely do not want to do bench press and all that gym bro crap' — and was around 6% body fat into his thirties on soccer alone. Nine months of intensive lower-body rehab after a knee injury, much of it kettlebell-based, with a physiotherapist who was also a former soccer player and personal trainer. Owns kettlebells and step-up equipment at home and travels with 12 kg bells. Currently trains weekly but on and off with no structure. Follows Trevor's videos and does some of the workouts.
prospect.medical: Grade 3 AC separation of the right shoulder from a 2017-18 fall, described as borderline surgical and left unrepaired on his surgeon's advice, followed by strength training and physical therapy. Completely torn left PCL from a cutting movement about two weeks after returning to soccer, diagnosed by MRI after eighteen months of self-treatment; no surgery, treated with nine months of rehab. One leg shorter than the other, with right hip pain that returns whenever he stops his band work. Cholesterol of 300 in 2020, brought well down through diet and supplements under a holistic cardiologist rather than pharmaceuticals, which he says also resolved morning joint pain, nocturia and frequent head colds. Year-round seasonal allergies, mouth breather, falls asleep in under a minute and breathes heavily at night; does not snore. Sleeps seven to eight hours.

signals: Successful and already largely fit; price was never a barrier and he anchored above it himself — 'How much does it cost? 20 grand?'
Good-to-great framing accepted explicitly: the rep's 'reclaiming the athlete that is already there inside you' drew 'Yep. Refine it.' and then 'Retune it.'
Health-literate and self-directed — manages cholesterol through a holistic cardiologist, knows glucose sequencing, still holds his old PT protocols
The gap he names is sequencing, not capability: 'I know what to do, but I don't know what order to get in, that's where I really need the guidance'
Not the preserver: he has substantial liquidity, could retire now, and wants to gain rather than hold on

goals.text: Get to roughly 10% body fat from 16-18%, and be shredded before turning 60
Be in optimal shape for the later stages of life — 'muscle mass is a predictor of longevity' and 'I don't want to wait till I'm 75 and can't do anything'
Not age the way his parents have at 80 — 'everything hurts, and I'm like, I don't want that'
Build real strength, the one thing he never trained because he hated conventional gym work
Learn the correct order and progression rather than more exercises — 'guidance on getting from point A to point B'
Stay physically capable enough to travel extensively in retirement with his fiancée

pains.text: Training is weekly but entirely unstructured — 'I do something every week, but it's on and off ... That's why I'm on the call with you'
Knows a large number of individual exercises but not the sequencing or progression to get from where he is to his goal
Hates conventional barbell and machine training and will not do it — the reason he never built strength despite twenty years around athletics
Belly fat he encounters daily and did not have for thirty-five years — 'when I feel it to just put my shoes on ... I'm like, I hate this'
Two significant unrepaired injuries constraining what he can load — a completely torn PCL and a grade 3 AC separation
Lost his rehab momentum through two house moves and getting engaged
Frequent long drives to Texas with substantial sitting and hotel gyms that may have one heavy kettlebell at best

offer.payment_plan_terms: Split in half at the rep's own suggestion: $3,000 immediately and $3,000 in 30 days, with no interest or uplift mentioned. Total remains $6,000.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: No refund guarantee was stated. Two commitments were made verbally: 'if you get an injury, we pause', and a performance reward the prospect found in the agreement himself — the rep described it as 'there's an award if you follow through the whole program. You get $500 for an accolable purchase.'

evidence: Payment taken live on the call via a Stripe link pasted into the Zoom chat — 'It says processing' then 'Done.' and the rep confirming 'Yep. Nice. I got it.'
Agreement email received, read and signed on the call: 'Okay, done.' and later 'I got a copy of the signed document'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked and confirmed for Tuesday at 5:15pm Eastern, with the prospect confirming the calendar invite in his inbox
Skool community invitation, TrueCoach access and the onboarding form all confirmed received on the call
Chose the six-month tier over twelve on the rep's recommendation and split payment at the rep's suggestion, not his own request
No counter-evidence: no hesitation, no objection at any point, and the prospect closed with 'I'm ready. Tired of doing this being lost.'
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor Tuesday 2 June at 5:15pm Eastern; prospect to complete the onboarding questionnaire; second payment of $3,000 due in 30 days

notable.note: The only close in the batch, the only complete Phase 11, and the only call with no pricing deviation — both tiers quoted correctly and the split was $3,000 plus $3,000 with no uplift. It is also the call where the consequence frame was never run at all, which is worth recording precisely because it closed: the prospect supplied his own urgency (parents at 80, the shredded man at the UPS store, muscle mass and longevity) and the rep never had to build any. Two things to watch. A 56-year-old with a completely torn PCL and an unrepaired grade 3 AC separation bought loaded kettlebell training with no clinician clearance sought, and he himself pointed out that the agreement disclaims injury liability. And two material terms — a pause-on-injury policy and a $500 completion reward — were surfaced by the prospect reading the contract rather than disclosed by the rep, who said of the reward 'I didn't go over that'. Separately, he reports falling asleep in under a minute, being a mouth breather and breathing heavily at night with year-round allergies; the rep probed for snoring and then let it go.

quality.notes: Persistent inversion throughout. The prospect's long injury narrative is repeatedly split across both labels, with the rep's label carrying the prospect's own account of his MRI and his doctor; conversely 'But why do you want to get shredded?' sits under the prospect. The exchange at 00:28:45 about the torn PCL is the least recoverable passage in the file — 'it was completely torn, okay, you can't tear it twice, okay, it was demolished' cannot be attributed with confidence to either speaker, and it is read here as most likely the prospect describing his own injury. The prospect's email address and full telephone number are spoken aloud and captured verbatim in the transcript.
